title: Moroccan Mint Tea Granita
changes_from_base: Sweet mint tea made with gunpowder green tea and orange blossom water replaces the strawberry purée.
summary: A refreshing frozen treat infused with gunpowder green tea, fresh mint and a hint of floral orange blossom water.
equipment: 20 cm square metal or glass dish

ingredients.item: fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped, plus a few to serve

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Bring 720 ml water to the boil in a saucepan. Add 6 g green tea, 30 g chopped mint and 75 g sugar, then simmer for 1 min.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Remove the pan from the heat and leave the mixture to steep for 12 min. Strain through a fine sieve into a jug and discard the leaves.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Leave to cool at room temperature for about 1 h, or speed it up by setting the jug in iced water for 25 min. Stir in 1 tsp orange blossom water if using.

steps.title: Initial freeze
steps.text: Pour the liquid into a 20 cm square dish and place in the freezer for about 1 h until the edges start to firm up.

steps.title: Scrape
steps.text: Use a fork to scrape the ice every 30 min for 2-3 h. Continue until you have a tray of fluffy crystals.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the crystals into glasses and serve straight away with fresh mint leaves.

tips: Use a metal dish to help the mixture freeze more quickly and evenly.
Ensure the tea is strained thoroughly to keep the texture of the crystals smooth.
Garnish with extra mint leaves for a bright and aromatic finish.
storage: Keep the granita covered in the freezer for up to 1 week and use a fork to break up the crystals before serving.
